title: Substrings Not Containing T as a Subsequence
statement:
You are given a string `S` and a short pattern string `T`, both made of lowercase English letters.

A string `P` is a **subsequence** of a string `W` if `P` can be obtained from `W` by deleting zero or more characters without changing the order of the remaining ones. The characters of `P` do not have to be adjacent in `W`.

Consider every non-empty **contiguous substring** of `S`. A substring is **good** if `T` is **not** a subsequence of it. Count the good substrings.

Substrings are counted by their position: two substrings with different start or end indices are different even if their text is identical. A string of length `n` has `n (n + 1) / 2` non-empty substrings.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the string `S`.
The second line contains the string `T`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of non-empty substrings of `S` that do not contain `T` as a subsequence.
constraints: `S` and `T` consist of lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: There are 15 substrings. Seven contain `ab` as a subsequence: `ab`, `abc`, `abca`, `abcab`, `bcab`, `cab` and the final `ab`. The other 8 are good: `a`, `b`, `c`, `a`, `b`, `bc`, `ca` and `bca`.
`b` never occurs, so all 10 substrings are good.
There are 3 substrings. Only the full string `ab` contains `ab`; `a` and `b` are good.

hints: Counting good substrings directly is hard; count, for each right end r, how many left ends l give a substring that does contain T, and subtract.
For a fixed r, the set of valid l is a prefix 0..g[r], where g[r] is the largest start index such that S[g..r] contains T. And g[r] never decreases as r grows.

Maintain best[j] = the largest start index l such that the first j characters of T are a subsequence of S[l..r]. When you read S[r], for every j with T[j-1] == S[r] (going from high j to low j) set best[j] = best[j-1], with best[0] defined as r. Then g[r] = best[|T|] and r - g[r] substrings ending at r are good.
